anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level SQL or transaction design forces the engine to process more rows, data, or time than business logic requires.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions serialize on hot buffer pages, latches, or page pins, throttling access despite sufficient overall memory.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Downstream replicas cannot receive, write, or replay the primary’s log stream fast enough, causing widening log-position and apply lag.

When all three root causes manifest together, the database exhibits extreme and wide-ranging distress: individual statements and whole transactions run long, saturating the buffer pool and generating spikes of buffer-busy and page-latch waits. CPU usage climbs yet throughput stalls as sessions spin on latches. Simultaneously, the primary’s write-ahead log grows rapidly and is retained because replicas fall behind; replica read staleness increases, failover readiness degrades, and log-shipping queues balloon. Monitoring views show the same costly SQL repeatedly in slow-query lists, elevated latch wait classes, and ever-increasing replication delay. These symptoms intertwine, making it difficult to attribute slow response times, memory pressure, or log growth to a single layer.

Causally, inefficient SQL amplifies logical I/O volume and concentrates access on a small working set (e.g., hot index root pages), driving buffer churn and latch contention. The stalled foreground sessions extend transaction lifetimes, yielding larger and burstier log batches that must traverse the replication pipeline. At the same time, latch contention and buffer thrashing on the primary slow log generation checkpoints, while replicas—already stressed by reapplying the same inefficient SQL—struggle to read hot pages fast enough, further widening replay lag. The growing log backlog prevents space reclamation on the primary, inflating the buffer cache footprint and intensifying contention. Thus, inefficient workload logic, internal buffer-manager contention, and replication apply bottlenecks form a reinforcing loop that degrades both primary performance and downstream consistency.

entry.official_description: Persisting SENSITIVE variables in encrypted form requires keyring component loaded through manifest file.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with file creation, filesystem access, write durability, log persistence, tablespace management, or storage-capacity boundaries.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect filesystem capacity and permissions, verify persistence paths, review log and data placement, and check whether storage latency or write failures are affecting the engine.
